approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It selects parents by score band and either makes a local mutation walk or combines connected fragments from two parents. Crossover cuts one non-ring single bond in each source, usually retains the larger first fragment and smaller donor fragment, and joins their endpoints with a single bond; an optional finishing mutation can follow. Ordinary mutation continuation remains active, while the direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identity and novelty checks form fresh surplus pools. A Gaussian process trained on all accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws choose the pool members that receive evaluations. Accepted offspring update the archive and breeding population. The crossover currently draws its donor without checking whether the two local attachment environments correspond.
approach.novelty: Construct a compatible donor fragment while keeping the already selected parent pair and first fragment. Enumerate the donor cuts, retain those whose endpoint contexts reciprocally match the two sides of the first cut, and sample them with their original relative probabilities. If there is no compatible choice, keep the original donor behavior. This targets actual attachment correspondence. The completed siblings removed retained components; earlier crossover experiments instead favored similar whole parents, retained the complete first-parent ring core, or rejected already constructed mismatches. The last approach nearly eliminated evaluated crossover, often leaving parent reproduction followed by mutation. This experiment keeps crossover opportunities and measures whether distinct compatible recombinants reach evaluation, without assuming that a matching rate or more local wins will improve final scores.

observed_bottleneck: The actual n-62daf219c70a summaries and run logs show a complete current-profile baseline with mean endpoint score 0.5956696497334577 and seed-macro population SD 0.02659287062806747. Its source independently samples the two cuts and checks the resulting molecular graph without comparing reciprocal attachment contexts. Published behavior includes 34334 crossover attempts and 1492 evaluated crossover descendants. Current isolated crossover removal n-767d2ce08797 lowers the complete matched mean by 0.054937284705486644 despite increasing strict local parent beats from 629 to 726 and incumbent gains from 258 to 282; the historical n-1faebb978a01 removal also loses score, but has a different Parent composition/profile and is not an additional current-profile replicate. The limitation targeted here is unconstrained donor attachment within a route whose current total contribution is supported, not an observed lack of crossover opportunities or evidence that crossover should be suppressed. Historical whole-parent similarity weighting n-a20706504e8f and first-parent ring retention n-822f049d9c70 activated yet lost 0.01597200876080433 and 0.015306780861481665, respectively, against their own Parent. Neither establishes the efficacy of actual endpoint correspondence. The reciprocal-context hard gate n-7ba291681388 supplies a precise predicate but cut evaluated crossover from 1133 to 29: 23 of 27 later-mutated crossover emissions first reproduced a parent, only six evaluated emissions had a changed immediate recombinant, and one task stopped early after an inherited identity error. Its incomplete apparent gain is not transferable efficacy evidence. The related n-32ac3137615b L07 composition remains partial: rejection-triggered mutation escalation has not been identified with L01 ordinary optional continuation. Only the documented cut predicate is reused.
hypothesis: Condition the retained connected-fragment crossover donor-cut distribution on reciprocal endpoint-context compatibility with the unchanged first-parent cut whenever compatible support exists, preserving the inherited donor behavior otherwise.

finding_summary.headline: Compatible donor sampling activated, but parent reproduction rose and mean score fell 0.020271
finding_summary.insights:
Constructing compatible donors avoided the earlier hard gate’s near-elimination of evaluated crossover, but retaining the route count did not retain its composition. Exact local correspondence often selected a fragment that rebuilt an existing parent; subsequent mutation then supplied novelty. This separates three claims that a matching percentage conceals: correct donor allocation, exposure to genuinely new recombination, and improvement of the complete search. The first is established, the second survives in a smaller channel with a clear task boundary, and the endpoint improvement prediction is contradicted. The experiment supports a negative mean contribution from this particular refinement under the tested composition; it does not overturn the separate evidence that crossover itself is useful.

Local correspondence also fails to certify chemistry. The output remains rich in aromatic, carbonyl and amine families, with conventional alternatives alongside reactive halogen bonds, doubtful ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. In the fluorinated family, fewer nitrogen-halogen molecules accompany more oxygen-halogen molecules, so one reduced alert would hide a changed liability. Finishing mutations can also remove the matched attachment environment. The useful next distinction is whether donor choices preserve favorable complete molecular relationships while producing a distinct, chemically credible product. Neither excluding reproduced parents nor filtering unusual bonds has been tested here. Which change in ancestry, pool competition or later feedback caused the endpoint loss remains open; the scored cohorts do not provide labels for unchosen donors.
finding_summary.results:
The conditional donor law worked exactly on 26,727 informative crossover attempts. On those same states, the inherited chance of a reciprocal context match averaged 9.55%; the applied law made it 100%. Independent reconstruction found no key, weighting, support, sampling or product-identity discrepancy. The resulting channel was usable: 354 compatible products that differed from both parents reached evaluation, including 257 pure crossovers. They produced 70 strict best-parent beats and 32 incumbent gains; 268 later served as parents. However, 22,117 of the 26,727 conditioned immediate products reproduced a parent. Of 850 evaluated conditioned descendants, 496 became novel only through finishing mutation. No informative nonidentical product reached evaluation in any of the three median-task runs.

Total crossover evaluations rose slightly from 1,492 to 1,549, but novel crossover pool entries fell from 29,730 to 22,962. Evaluations following genuinely nonidentical immediate crossover fell from 1,368 to 1,023, and pure crossovers fell from 961 to 725. All fifteen task runs completed, with every announced batch valid and unique. The complete matched endpoint mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.575399, a change of -0.020271 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.061941, +0.019643 and -0.018514; ten of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined. Seed population SD fell from 0.026593 to 0.008463. Overall local parent beats nevertheless increased from 629 to 654, and incumbent gains from 258 to 277.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain unusual halogen bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-eb61315a5619 produces compact indole-derived amides and aryl ketones, linked nitrogen-rich heterocycles, aryl-substituted aliphatic amines, diaryl macrocyclic amides and other connected nitrogen/carbonyl rings, and fluorinated fused imino/carbonyl heterocycles. This is substantial ring chemistry, with narrower leading families within individual seeds. It is neither ring-deficient nor globally scaffold-collapsed. The digest ring-closure-string incidence ranges from 0.9759 to 0.9920 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.9736 to 0.9862; these are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. Stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0 on every task. Formal-charge-string incidence is 0.0011 for median_2 and 0.0 elsewhere, although recognizable protonatable aliphatic amines occur. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory paths were present and read. Each objective has 900 records, including 870 optimizer observations, in each node. No objective, issued Search seed or Parent path is missing: context.comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. The comparison is against the published n-62daf219c70a seed directories, not a historical profile or a partial panel. Initial rows are excluded from the descriptor counts below. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 perception of the trajectory SMILES gives Child median heavy-atom counts of 25, 35, 36, 32 and 27 in the fixed objective order, versus Parent medians of 25, 33, 31, 30 and 27. Rich rings and ordinary amide, ether and amine groups coexist with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, reactive peripheral groups, cyclic alkynes or cumulenes and difficult bridges. The aggregate judgment is questionable synthetic plausibility and weak drug-likeness, with real counterexamples of more conventional chemistry. Scores and SMILES alone do not establish stability, synthesis, conformations, protonation or biological activity. The task gradients below are descriptive associations and explicitly do not attribute a chemical feature to donor conditioning, mutation or any component. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals; the full trajectories supplied the other seed endpoints and show that the final proposal need not be the incumbent. Exact record provenance, descriptors and path hashes are in .slots/r0016-01-improve-L01/molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json. Quoted SMILES come only from the Child digest or trusted Child citation paths; Parent comparisons cite published seed/evaluation records descriptively. The recurring gaps retain provenance in n-c55c3d520a2c through the published n-62daf219c70a assessment. That historical provenance is not an additional matched replica.

per_task.generated_character: The seed leaders have 25-26 heavy atoms. Seed 0 makes a pyrrole-containing fused system with a seven-membered nitrogen ring, an N-bromo aryl amide, phenol and bromomethyl substituent. Seeds 1 and 2 favor substituted indole-like aromatic systems: an N-fluoro aryl amide with an N-hydroxy ring nitrogen in seed 1, and an aryl ketone with N-fluoro ring nitrogen, imine and methylamino groups in seed 2. These are mostly compact aromatic/carbonyl frameworks; the high-score region is not short acyclic fragments. The output median is 25 heavy atoms, unchanged from Parent. Parent leaders are also indole-related aryl carbonyl families with N-halogen attachments, including a pyridyl N-hydroxy amide, a vicinal diketone and a cumulene-containing analogue. Local nitrogen and halogen bonding, rather than an absence of rings or familiar amide chemistry, makes the Child targets questionable to synthesize and handle.
liabilities: N-Br/N-Cl amides and N-F/N-Cl/N-Br ring nitrogens must be distinguished from ordinary aryl C-halogen substitution. Direct N-halogen bonds occur in 490 of 870 Child optimizer observations versus 445 of 870 Parent observations.
Halomethyl groups, imines and N-O substitution add environment-dependent reactivity concerns. Their occurrence in high-scoring structures is not a stability or synthetic-accessibility result.
The expanded fused nitrogen ring of the seed-0 leader is an additional geometry and synthetic-route question; compact atom count does not resolve it.
missing_features: Conventional nitrogen substitution that retains the strongest compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement is not consistently represented among the leaders: all 50 highest optimizer observations carry a direct N-halogen bond. The non-N-halogen indole amide is a counterexample to complete incapacity.

Independent, synthetically credible compact alternatives to the leading indole-derived families remain limited; the record does not identify an exact missing target pharmacophore or support simply adding more rings or donors.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145; the seed-0 N-bromo amide leader reaches 0.44989726212142783 at evaluation 283. Seed-1 and seed-2 leaders reach 0.4403336603489188 and 0.4197178065554812. Multiple peripheral halogen/halomethyl variants tie at 0.4478476056206344, so their particular reactive substituents are not distinguished by those labels. A 25-heavy-atom N-H indole amide with only carbon-bound halogens scores 0.4086104282862019 at seed 1/evaluation 188: useful reward is possible without an N-halogen bond. Methane scores 0.0, but a 48-heavy-atom doubled aromatic amidine framework also scores only 2.0463489242471772e-20. The visible association is compact, organized aromatic/carbonyl chemistry, not maximum ring count, size or halogen count. Matched Parent endpoints are 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081 for seeds 0, 1 and 2; the Child changes which local family is favored without consistently resolving the Parent liabilities.

per_task.generated_character: Child leaders have 32-38 heavy atoms. Seed 1 connects aza-aromatic rings and a carbonyl/oxygen heterocycle to an aryl thione system with a perceived four-membered ring, nitrile, aryl fluorine, chloromethyl and an alkynyl alkyl appendage. Seed 0 instead gives densely fused nitrogen-rich dione systems with an N-S-butyl connection; seed 2 has extensively cross-linked azaaryl/ester/ether rings. The output median rises from Parent 33 to Child 35 heavy atoms, and the median RDKit-perceived ring count from 4 to 6. Very large aromatic concatenations coexist with these leaders. The best seed-1 structures have carbon-bound halogens rather than N/O-halogen bonds, a real difference from the Parent seed-0 leader with O-F and halomethyl ether chemistry. That local difference does not make the small-ring thione, cyclic alkyne variants or dense ring junctions straightforward synthetic targets.
liabilities: Seed 1/evaluation 293 contains an alkyne inside a five-membered ring at the same score as its open-chain relatives. RDKit acceptance is not evidence that such a strained ring is a stable synthetic target.
The aryl-thione region contains a small ring, and other seeds introduce dense fused/bridged azaaromatic connectivity or N-S substitution; these require environment-specific feasibility assessment.
All 50 highest Child optimizer observations lack direct N/O-halogen bonds, yet substantial geometry concerns persist. A single bond-alert count would miss them.
missing_features: The record lacks a consistently accessible realization of the favorable linked heterocyclic arrangement with controlled ring geometry; many leading Child variants replace one liability with difficult small-ring or bridged connectivity.

The Parent seed-0 favorable compact combination is not recovered at its score in any Child seed. The visible labels support sensitivity to a particular arrangement, not a claim that general aromatic or nitrogen richness is missing.
Stereochemical identity is absent for potentially stereogenic attachment centres in the leading linked and cross-linked families.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. A 20-heavy-atom aryl ether/azaaryl proposal scores 0.5184097484001051, while the seed-1 linked heterocyclic leader and several substitutions score 0.6376977895881145. An acyclic terminal alkyne variant, a saturated alkyl variant and a five-membered cyclic alkyne variant all receive that same score. The supplied labels therefore do not distinguish the severe geometric concern introduced by closing the alkyne into that small ring. A 103-heavy-atom, highly aromatic concatenation scores 0.5848326652372517, and tiny Cl/Br/OF species sit at 0.5; neither elaborate size nor the floor value establishes useful chemistry. The Child seed-0 and seed-2 leaders score 0.619323504758148 and 0.6187978068097204. Published Parent endpoints are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013. The Parent seed-0 compact linked heterocycle achieved its much higher label despite O-F/thione/halomethyl liabilities. Thus more Child ring richness and fewer heteroatom-halogen bonds do not demonstrate recovery of that favorable chemical arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are aryl-substituted aliphatic amines, with 25-33 heavy atoms. Seed 0 has a flexible aminoalkyl chain and an N-methylaziridine on an aromatic ether framework. Seed 1 has a tertiary dialkylamine and primary amine attached to a bromophenolic partially saturated polycycle. Seed 2 combines a brominated anisole with small bridged carbon/nitrogen rings, another cyclic amine, bromomethyl substitution and a sulfoxide-linked aryl group. Available aliphatic amines are already abundant; the zero formal-charge-string rate does not mean the molecules lack basic centres. The Child median rises to 36 heavy atoms from Parent 31, with median halogen count 4 versus 3. The Parent leaders include flexible aryl tertiary amines and recognizable pyrrolidine/fused-thioether or aminoalkyl cyclic-amine frameworks. Child seed 1 also supplies a comparatively conventional aminated saturated-ring example without small rings, so synthetic plausibility is mixed rather than uniformly poor.
liabilities: The seed-0 aziridine and seed-2 network of small rings and bridges raise strain, reactivity and synthetic-route concerns that neutral valence-valid SMILES do not settle.
Bromomethyl/chloromethyl substitution and substantial halogen mass remain in leading families; the seed-2 best molecule has a calculated molecular weight of about 599.364 despite only 33 heavy atoms.

Aromaticity and amine functionality alone do not establish solubility, chemical stability or biological selectivity. The comparatively conventional seed-1 molecule is a counterexample to treating all high-scoring outputs as chemically implausible.
missing_features: Defined stereochemical forms are missing for the successful saturated and bridged arrangements: every one of the 50 highest Child observations has at least one RDKit-perceived unassigned stereocentre.

Consistent access to less strained, less heavily elaborated realizations of the useful aryl/amine presentation remains unresolved. The seed-1 precursor and Parent families demonstrate that the generator can already make such alternatives.

A missing basic nitrogen is not supported by this output. Protonation, conformational accessibility and the value of specific stereoisomers remain unmeasured rather than established score requirements.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: A dichloroaryl methyl sulfone scores 0.00032141189568530486, and an N-sulfonyl cyclic amine with amide and sulfur-linked carbonyl substituents scores 0.0003556511895523401. The free aliphatic-amine/aryl leaders reach 0.9595962046462246, 0.9885614466214269 and 0.9946639086633907 in seeds 0, 1 and 2. The seed-1 aminated fused-ring precursor at evaluation 253 scores 0.9843400397587724 without three- or four-membered rings or N/O-halogen bonds. High reward therefore does not require the most crowded Child cages or reactive halogen bonding. The association is an available aliphatic amine presented with aromatic and hydrophobic regions, not nitrogen or halogen count alone. Matched Parent endpoints are 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012 using the more recognizable flexible/cyclic amine families. These are supplied benchmark labels, not measured affinity, selectivity, protonation or synthetic feasibility.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 best molecule is a 31-heavy-atom diaryl framework closed by a 14-membered ring containing ether and two amide connections, with ethoxy, N-propyl/N-methyl and carbon-methyl substituents. Its two aromatic rings and recognizable amide/ether chemistry are more conventional than the reactive-halogen leaders elsewhere; macrocyclization, conformational control and stereochemical definition remain unproven. Seed 0 instead couples a fused azaaromatic/tertiary-amine region to a dicarbonyl nitrogen ring. Seed 2 uses a more unusual conjugated fused system with small nitrogen rings and imide-like carbonyls. Leaders have 30-34 heavy atoms. The Child median is 32 heavy atoms versus Parent 30, while median perceived ring count decreases from 5 to 4. The Parent also expresses aryl or azaaryl surfaces with nitrogen/carbonyl rings, often in more bridged architectures. The Child best is consequently a meaningful topology counterexample to an inevitable drift toward greater ring count.
liabilities: The leading macrocycle has familiar bonds but still requires a feasible ring-closing route and conformational control; this report does not classify macrocycles themselves as implausible.
Other leading families include small nitrogen rings, unusual exocyclic conjugation and connected medium rings, which present different geometric problems from the best macrocycle.
N/O-halogen-free chemistry is already possible: all 50 highest Child observations lack those bonds. All 50 nevertheless retain at least one perceived unassigned stereocentre.
missing_features: Reliable chemically independent realizations of the useful aromatic/amide/ether arrangement are limited among leaders within a seed, despite the distinct successful macrocycle and azaaromatic families across seeds.

The macrocycle carbon stereocentre and potentially stereogenic connected-ring centres remain unassigned. Conformational and synthetic access to their functional-group arrangement has not been demonstrated.

The visible record identifies no exact missing target motif and no shortage of rings, carbonyls or nitrogen. Its residual gap is quality and coverage of complete arrangements rather than another isolated functional group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329; an early aryl ether/azaaryl proposal scores 0.11709181070641599 and methane scores 0.0. The seed-1 diaryl bis-amide macrocycle reaches 0.2402384598457076. Changing N-propyl to N-methyl in the same macrocyclic organization gives 0.23908544035545837; extending the ether-side ring segment gives 0.23834846924966485. These near values favor the combined aromatic, amide and ether organization rather than one exact short side chain. A 63-heavy-atom polyaromatic concatenation scores only 0.12412200802325507, so extra aromatic mass is not a solution in this sample. Child seed-0 and seed-2 endpoints are 0.2178360563647521 and 0.2148566343031069. Matched Parent endpoints are 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.22600312875247064. The relatively conventional Child macrocycle improves its seed label, while different seeds retain more difficult topologies and lower endpoints; this is conditional scaffold evidence, not a general score advantage for macrocycles.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2 produces a 27-heavy-atom fused nitrogen-rich imino/carbonyl heterocycle with N-methyl groups, attached to a fluorinated unsaturated carbocycle and a difluoromethyl ether-bearing alkenyl group. Its best examples include both a five-membered carbocycle and a four-membered relative, each bearing O-F. Seed 0 has a related imino/carbonyl system with fluorinated small carbocycles, thiol/N-S substitution and a carbonyl-O-F group. Seed 1 instead retains a fused dione, an unsaturated nitrogen ring and fluorinated enolic/alkenyl substitution with no direct N/O-halogen bond. The median size is 27 heavy atoms in both Child and Parent. The Parent seed-2 leader was a different aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring attached to a small cyclic cumulene; other Parent leaders carried N-F. The Child best avoids a cyclic cumulene but retains an O-F liability, so the chemical concern has changed rather than disappeared.
liabilities: Direct O-halogen bonds occur in 306 of 870 Child optimizer observations versus 83 of 870 Parent observations, while direct N-halogen bonds decrease from 476 to 79. Tracking only N-halogen incidence would hide a change of liability.
The Child best has O-F rather than merely ordinary carbon-bound fluorine. Its carbonyl-O-F, thiol, N-S and dithiocarboxyl relatives carry separate environment-dependent reactivity concerns.

There are 33 Child observations with RDKit-perceived cyclic cumulated carbon centres, versus 40 in Parent. They are not necessary for the best Child score, but five-membered cyclic cumulenes remain an explicit geometry concern.
The seed-1 leader is a genuine counterexample to universal N/O-halogen or cyclic-cumulene dependence; its unsaturated nitrogen ring and stereochemistry still need their own assessment.
missing_features: The strongest compact fluorinated/polar organization is not consistently realized with conventional stable bond environments. Seed 1 proves non-N/O-halogen alternatives exist, but not at the Child seed-2 leading label.

Geometrically credible unsaturation and fully specified stereochemical identity remain missing from many high-scoring variants; useful noncumulated examples already occur, so a missing ability to make saturated or ordinary unsaturated rings would be an overstatement.
The tautomeric and conformational identity of imino, enolic and unsaturated nitrogen-ring forms is unresolved. No exact unseen target pharmacophore can be inferred from these scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298; an early expanded carbonyl-rich fused heterocycle scores 7.244639250726666e-27, and isolated F scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. The compact fluorinated seed-2 leader at evaluation 189 reaches 0.6630528172128829, as does the different small-ring/alkenyl arrangement at evaluation 210. Introducing cumulated double bonds into the five-membered ring at evaluation 242 gives 0.6203783245899045: the cyclic cumulene is unnecessary for the Child best. Replacing the carbonyl by imino in the four-membered relative gives 0.6493152838415691; extending its difluoromethyl ether to a fluorinated two-carbon substituent gives 0.5167651236214245. The visible gradient is sensitive to compact fluorinated/polar organization, not fluorine count alone. Child seed-0 and seed-1 endpoints are 0.5707010469643454 and 0.5957108223717572; the latter has no N/O-halogen or cyclic cumulene. Matched Parent endpoints are 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067 and 0.7208853668418119. Neither the higher Parent cyclic-cumulene label nor the Child O-F-rich leaders prove that those liabilities are required.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced in the published n-62daf219c70a assessment and independently re-observed in n-eb61315a5619 under the supplied current profile, Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, and 300 observations per objective. Compact aromatic/carbonyl leaders retain N-halogen bonds, while a fluorinated family changes from Parent 476 to Child 79 N-halogen observations but from 83 to 306 O-halogen observations out of 870. High-scoring aryl amines, a diaryl bis-amide macrocycle and a fluorinated dione without N/O-halogen bonds show that conventional alternatives already occur. Local matching and a reduction in one alert therefore do not establish chemical quality.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond chemistry while retaining favorable complete molecular arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs transformations that distinguish bond environment and intact functional-group context, while offering conventional alternatives to reactive attachments without erasing useful aromatic, carbonyl or amine arrangements. Assess the full set of emitted environments so that one liability is not merely replaced by another. These output associations do not attribute the chemistry to a component or establish that a blanket filter improves scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source n-c55c3d520a2c via the published n-62daf219c70a assessment; independently present in n-eb61315a5619 on the complete current-profile Search panel at 300 observations per objective. Child output includes a five-membered cyclic alkyne tied with open-chain and saturated relatives, small cyclic cumulenes, and densely connected small-ring amine frameworks. Counterexamples include a noncumulated fluorinated leader, an aryl amine without small rings and a recognizable amide/ether macrocycle. Rich ring counts are not the missing capability.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish representable ring connectivity from credible ring geometry and unsaturation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need ring-size, bond-geometry and bridge-connectivity awareness, with feasible alternate topologies that preserve functional relationships supported by current feedback. A successful molecular graph check or aromatic label is insufficient. Do not infer a universal prohibition of small rings, fused rings or macrocycles; the observed counterexamples and absence of geometry measurements limit this to a feasibility gap, with no demonstrated component-specific or causal score benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally reported for n-c55c3d520a2c and carried by n-62daf219c70a, this persists in n-eb61315a5619 on Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the current profile and 300 observations per objective. Every digest stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0. Read-only RDKit perception finds unassigned stereocentres in 2661 of 4350 Child optimizer observations, compared with 2408 of 4350 Parent observations, including aryl amines, fluorinated small rings and macrocyclic amides. These counts concern perceived centres, not measured configurational stability.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereochemical identity unspecified after creating potentially stereogenic saturated and connected-ring centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations should preserve or resolve stereochemical identity where chemically meaningful, while treating achiral and configurationally unstable cases appropriately. Charge state and tautomerism require separate handling: neutral notation does not mean a basic centre is absent. The trajectories establish an identity gap, not a measured stereochemical score penalty or evidence that any particular retained component caused it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source n-c55c3d520a2c through the published n-62daf219c70a assessment; re-observed in n-eb61315a5619 on the matched current-profile Search panel at 300 observations per objective. Child still emits 47 molecules with at most three heavy atoms among 4350 optimizer observations, although Parent emitted 99. Tiny fragments often have floor or near-floor labels, while a 48-heavy-atom doubled aromatic framework and a 103-heavy-atom aromatic concatenation fail to match their corresponding compact leaders. Conversely, a smaller aryl amine and the moderately sized macrocycle retain high labels. The smaller fragment count is a real counterexample to a universal worsening claim.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain useful functional-group context while controlling fragmentation and excessive molecular elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use accepted task-local feedback to preserve useful combinations of chemical regions when shrinking, expanding or reconnecting a molecule. Allow meaningful simplification and growth; neither a fixed minimum size nor a preference for larger structures follows from these examples. The evidence describes residual context control under this Parent and profile, not attribution to crossover or a proven gain from a size rule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by n-62daf219c70a, this remains conditional evidence in n-eb61315a5619 under the supplied current profile, Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, and 300 observations per objective. Leading series repeatedly change short substituents, halogen attachment, ring size or carbonyl/imino identity while retaining the same aromatic/carbonyl organization. Different seeds nevertheless reach distinct fused, flexible-amine and macrocyclic families, and the Child supplies genuinely different ring connectivities. Thus the observation is narrow useful alternatives within local families, not global collapse or inability to generate rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has limited consistent access to chemically independent plausible alternatives within a successful local scaffold family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide alternative scaffold connectivities that preserve favorable functional relationships learned from the current observations, and examine their chemical credibility as well as their labels. Distinct SMILES and higher ring counts do not alone demonstrate useful coverage. This is a conditional generator capability gap; no objective identity, preselected target scaffold, specific component attribution or guaranteed benefit from more diversity is supported.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
